💡 Key Takeaways
  • Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday.
  • Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.
  • Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.

Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.

According to recent reports, the Senate Judiciary Committee’s panel on Crime and Counterterrorism held the hearing after its Chairman Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and ranking member Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., introduced a bill Monday that would ban pre-dispute arbitration agreements from affecting cases where a minor was harmed online, including by sexual exploitation.

Sources indicate that hawley and Durbin also worked together on a separate bill to expand eligibility for victims of abuse to bring civil suits against online platforms that intentionally, knowingly or recklessly promoted or facilitated the abuse. It would also include penalties for certain platforms that fail to report child pornography violations on their sites.

Recent findings suggest that that bill is included in a manager’s amendment to the Senate’s fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill. Durbin encouraged Congress to pass the NDAA “in the closing days” of the session because “protecting children is an notable part of it.”.

Sources indicate that “I have a few weeks left in my service in the United States Senate,” said Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January. “I’m thinking each day it’s coming to an end, but I want it to come [to an] end the right way.”.

The subcommittee has spent much of the 119th Congress focused on harms to children online, including from artificial intelligence chatbots.

Tuesday’s hearing included testimony from survivors and experts on child exploitation on Roblox.

Hawley noted that victims are bound by pre-dispute agreements with Roblox to settle claims through private arbitration, rather than in court.

“They slam the courthouse door shut in their faces,” Hawley said. “We’re talking about children now, child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very firm that has exposed them to the content to begin with.”.

A spokesperson for Roblox stated in a statement that “safety has been central” to the platform since its launch.

“We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” the spokesperson said. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”.

Industry observers note that myriam Gilles, a professor of law at Northwestern University, told the panel that a 2022 law that ended forced arbitration agreements for victims of sexual assault has gaps. She said Roblox has argued it does not apply to online actions, just “completed physical assault” and does not apply to platforms.

She also said that Hawley’s new arbitration bill would enhance the effects of his measure regarding civil suits by making sure those suits can be heard publicly if families so choose.

“Congress can pass laws, but if [suits] just get shunted into private arbitration, they’re doing no good in the world,” Gilles mentioned. “A right to sue that ends in secret arbitration is a right in name only.”.

The hearing came the same day that advocates, including reality TV personality and activist Paris Hilton, held a press conference to urge House action on a bill (S 1837) that would allow individuals to bring civil suits over nonconsensual intimate depictions generated by artificial intelligence or for possession or production of deepfake porn if there was also intent to disclose the images.

That bill passed the Senate in January but has not been taken up in the House.

#65601. Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1007 w)

Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

Hill GOP looking to trim White House's $50 billion aviation ask

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.
  • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s new ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.

The original ask contained roughly $12 billion that was tied directly to air traffic control upgrades, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said, with the remainder going toward long-sought airport terminal and other upgrades to aging aviation facilities.

Duffy and Vought laid out in a letter to House and Senate appropriators on Tuesday what the extra $20 billion would be for — half for construction of five fresh air route traffic control centers, and half for construction, replacement and improvement of up to 140 air traffic control towers.

Industry observers note that they justified the increased demand because of the “urgent need” that became evident after the ground stop. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford fanned out across the Capitol to try to sell the request, including a stop at Senate Republicans’ weekly policy lunch.

But it promptly became evident that their own allies on Capitol Hill want more and better justification for why so much extra money is needed.

Not only are there concerns that much of the request would go to terminal reconstruction and other longer-term projects, but lawmakers keep noting the FAA hasn’t yet spent about $8 billion out of the initial $12.5 billion “down payment” on air traffic control modernization provided in last year’s budget reconciliation law.

“I don’t think the full $50 billion will be funded,” Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said Tuesday. “What we just discussed there, and what I expressed, is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.”.

Still, Cruz mentioned the administration had done a “good job” with the initial $12.5 billion modernization initiative so far and he expected to see continued bipartisan support for the effort.

Senate Republicans are considering adding additional aviation funds through a filibuster-proof reconciliation bill, a process that could begin as soon as this week with a floor “vote-a-rama” on a resolution to unlock that process. Cruz remarked that while reconciliation could be the vehicle used, additional aviation funds need to be “safety-focused.”.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., remarked after the lunch with Duffy and Bedford that he expects Congress will look at a package more in the $10 billion to $30 billion range.

For his part, Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., noted the airline industry itself should foot at least a portion of the bill, considering how much federal support the carriers have received over the years.

“I don't understand why the airline industry doesn't pay for it. We give them unbelievable amounts of money,” Scott stated, adding that he doesn’t like adding to the deficit and is “not significant on government running things.”.

Duffy explained the need for the high price tag as the result of decades of pent-up demand that are now threatening major disruptions and safety risks to the traveling public.

It has been revealed that “This has never been done. To be clear, we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment that’s been a problem for decades,” he said. “I and the president have decided we are going to lean in and fix it.”.

According to recent reports, he called the effort a “historic investment” reflecting the ways air travel has changed since much of the nation’s infrastructure was built — noting that the newest tower was constructed in 1969 and much of the software being used is from the 1990s. Still, Duffy remarked, on the current course of funding, it would take 300 years to replace every U.S. tower.

Sources indicate that “I'm not going to tell [Congress] how to do their work, but I'm telling everybody what we need,” Duffy mentioned. “And whether it's a party-line vote or if it's a bipartisan vote, I do think this is one moment in a very charged political environment — one moment where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in to do this.”.

Even as Duffy petitioned for additional funds Tuesday, he stated that the “root cause” of the equipment instability that made the ground stop necessary is still unclear as investigators analyze the router that caused the problem.

A “routine switchover” from old copper wires to digital fiber in the telecommunications system “started to create concerns in our network,” Duffy explained Tuesday.

The telecommunications transition includes the conversion of thousands of routers to what are known as Juniper devices — a process being undertaken by contractor L3Harris Technologies. Duffy and Bedford explained that 68 other routers had been converted without incident prior to the problematic switchover Friday.

Bedford stated Tuesday that use of the router that officials have identified as the source of the system instability has been suspended “and we've disabled the ones that are out there.”.

It has been revealed that the decision to suspend use of the router followed an inquiry sent to the agency by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats a day prior. “With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding safety and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” they wrote.

Sources indicate that bedford said he was “highly confident” that similar problems wouldn’t erupt again. “Every element of this is going to be analyzed to see what we learn here and make sure that it doesn't get repeated,” he said.

David Jordan, Lia Chien and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

American Airlines aims to refresh and expand its three Admirals Club lounges at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport.

The carrier mentioned Tuesday that it will add seating, upgrade amenities, and improve food and beverage service across all three spaces in Terminal 4.

In the near term, the Admirals Club lounge in Concourse A between gates A19 and A21 will get a upcoming servery area, infrastructure enhancements to support expanded food and beverage offerings, and facility updates to improve the overall customer experience.

Sources indicate that longer-term intends call for nearly tripling the combined footprint of the Concourse A lounges, the other being above gates A7-A9. Newly introduced furniture and finishings will be brought in, and seating capacity will expand by 150%.

The lounge in Concourse B, between gates B5 and B7, will get a fresh self-service food and beverage area and have its seating capacity increased by 20%.

“Phoenix continues to be an notable hub in our network, and these investments reflect our commitment to giving customers more space, comfort, and convenience when they travel through PHX,” American Chief Customer Officer Heather Garboden remarked in a news release. “While we look forward to the development of the new West Terminal, these enhancements will help create an even more seamless travel experience for the millions of customers who pass through Phoenix each year.”.

In a recent development, the planned West Terminal will be built on the west side of the airport between Terminal 3 and Taxiway U. American is expected to serve as the terminal’s primary carrier.

According to the airport’s timeline, the project should be finished by 2033.

TAP Air Portugal will launch a newly introduced route to Washington, D.C., next year.

Starting March 30, 2027, the carrier will connect Porto and Washington Dulles. Flights will operate three times weekly.

It has been revealed that presently, TAP serves Dulles from its hub at Humberto Delgado Airport in Lisbon. Its only U.S.-bound routes from Porto are to Boston and Newark, Newly introduced Jersey.

TAP serves Porto via Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport.

The carrier serves nine destinations in the U.S., the others being Newly introduced York-JFK, Chicago O’Hare, Orlando, Florida, Miami, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.

Breaking: Senate Dems dismiss talk of earlier leadership election; Schumer confident

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that senate Minority Leader Charles E.
  • Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a newly introduced majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec.
  • That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a newly introduced majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec. 1.

That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.

The prospect of an earlier vote had been floated as a way to prevent internal divisions from hobbling the incoming majority before the 120th Congress even began.

But supporters of Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., both in the chamber and among party activists outside it, were increasingly casting the idea of a shorter contest as a bid to halt momentum for his bid against Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

Even as Schumer maintained that he has the votes necessary to be elected as majority leader, several senators insisted Tuesday the discussion taking place within the caucus was a good thing.

According to recent reports, “I’m confident I’ll be the next leader. I have the votes,” Schumer told reporters on Tuesday following the conference’s lunch.

Van Hollen for his part told reporters Tuesday he believes his bid has “momentum at this point in time, which is why there was an effort to short-circuit the process.”.

“And fortunately, I think that will fail.”.

Several senators leaving the meeting said the topic of the leadership contest did not come up at all, and that neither Van Hollen nor Schumer gave a presentation regarding their bids.

Recent findings suggest that that was in large part due to the absence of the incoming senators — which could be as high as 13, depending on how the dust settles in Alaska — who are able to vote in the leadership elections. Retiring senators do not cast a ballot.

With such a large class of incoming freshman, several incumbents saw it crucial to keep the election scheduled as is.

It has been revealed that “No one has ever raised that with me. I mean, I saw a rumor that some were wanting to contemplate that,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Tuesday after the meeting. “The leadership discussions did not come up today. And part of the reason is we didn’t have the newcomers.”.

“Remember, they all get a vote in the leadership discussion, and it would be hard to get them here,” Kaine continued, noting that only Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., was present for Tuesday’s lunch amid his belated orientation. “But nobody else was here, and that discussion needs to have the newcomers because newcomers get votes. The outgoers don’t, right?”.

Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. echoed that sentiment on Monday evening, saying, “I want to hear from the freshman class as well.”.

Industry observers note that sen. Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, mentioned, “I don’t know that” when asked about moving up the elections. “I think that we need to make sure that there’s enough time for what I would call a robust discussion about what we’re going to do. I think we should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here, and I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard.

“They’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table,” she said.

Several senators-elect are among those who have publicly thrown their hats into Van Hollen’s corner, including Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.El-Sayed on Tuesday mentioned at The Atlantic Summit that he sees Van Hollen as “unique” in his experience in the Senate and running the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as well as what he called “a willingness to take risks.”.

“We need people who are willing to take legislative risk,” he said. “We need to rethink the way we legislate. It just should not be the process where you make one or two omnibus pieces of legislation that nobody really knows what’s in them,” he continued, advocating for piecemeal legislation.

It has been revealed that but there are about 15 Democrats who have publicly backed Schumer’s bid. If former Rep. Mary Peltola maintains her lead in the lone outstanding Senate race in Alaska, Schumer would need 29 to secure the helm of the ship.

“I committed to Sen. Schumer literally months ago, and I continue to support him,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., mentioned Monday. “I’m incredibly excited about the new ideas that our new colleagues have, and their energy, and the potential for changing the way we operate in the Senate, which we have to do because we need to be more effective.”.

In a recent development, several incumbents have also thrown their support behind Van Hollen for leadership change, including Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.“I think, as I’ve stated many times, the American people want change in the way we do business here in Washington, and I think Chris Van Hollen would be a great leader of the Democrats,” Sanders said Monday.

Several senators and senators-elect are refusing to comment publicly on who they’ll back.

Recent findings suggest that that included Sen. Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., who said he wants “to hear the commitments from folks that are pursuing this leadership role as well as every leadership position in the Senate, as well as chairs of committees, to what their commitments are to having a strong agenda that’s going to improve people’s lives.”.

Kaine is also in that camp, and insisted Monday he hadn’t made up his mind. But he did speak positively of Schumer’s recruiting efforts in the midterms and history of dealing with a Trump White House.

“Schumer just delivered a major win for us. No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer,” he said. “Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in the caucus, and dealing with this wounded president is going to be a challenge over the next few years.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change,” he noted. “So we got to figure that out as a caucus, and we’re going to be able to. And we’re not afraid to have a discussion because we’re Democrats. We like democracy.”.

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., also remained mum on who he’ll support but said, “You can’t argue” Schumer brought Democrats the majority.

“I think it’s a healthy thing to try and improve how the conference goes about its business,” he noted. “I don’t think that is a distraction. We can deal with some distractions. We have to keep our eye on the ball.”.

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who last week called for upcoming leadership in a news conference with Sanders, days before Van Hollen’s announcement, was noncommittal arriving to the Capitol on Monday if that meant she’d be supporting the Maryland Democrat.

Senate Democrats’ election will most likely be a secret ballot. And most senators remained unified against moving the leadership elections before they recess for the Thanksgiving break.

Industry observers note that “They should not be moved up. There was a reason that those rule changes took place before, and they should take place in December,” Lujan said.

Kaine dismissed Van Hollen’s challenge as anything unusual.

“We’re Democrats. It’s frankly unusual that there usually [aren’t] challenges to Democratic leaders because we’re Democrats,” he said. “It’s been a little unusual to have been here for 13 years and not really have them like this. But I think it’s a discussion not just about the two contenders for the leader role, but also the leadership team and priorities, and it’s all wrapped up in one discussion.”.

“That’s why we decided, don’t do these votes until December, because you want to let the election settle and understand exactly what’s up, and then hear from potential votes.”.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said, “I think we should stick with the rules when it comes to the caucus. … That’s going to be what makes sure that we show that we have a real process.”.

Sanders asked: “Why would anyone want to do that?” when asked.

“I think there’s a date that’s been called, and that should be the date.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, waiting more than two hours for your checked bag is frustrating. Watching it emerge covered in a brown substance that looks like human waste is considerably worse. That is what American Airlines passengers reported in Atlanta this week, though the airline says the mess had a much less revolting explanation: peanut butter.

    Passengers aboard American Airlines flight 2609 from Miami (MIA) to Atlanta (ATL) on November 16, 2026, reported an unpleasant surprise at baggage claim. Travelers waited more than two hours before their luggage appeared on carousel eight at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. When the bags arrived, passengers saw a brown substance smeared across them and naturally feared the worst.

    Passenger Derick McCallum recorded the scene and later questioned the airline’s explanation:.

    According to recent reports, “Even if somebody did pack peanut butter? How much peanut butter does somebody pack to cover that many bags?”.

    (my mind goes to Diddy Combs and AstroGlide…).

    American later said that liquefied peanut butter had leaked from a passenger’s checked bag, affecting nearby luggage. The airline said an environmental inspection confirmed its explanation.

    “Unfortunately, a food item from a customer’s checked bag leaked during the flight, affecting several bags nearby.”.

    I would certainly prefer peanut butter to the alternative passengers feared. But I would still be rather unhappy about finding someone else’s sandwich spread having spoiled my suitcase.

    It isn’t clear how much peanut butter was involved, how it was packaged, or exactly how it spread…feel free to speculate.

    Passengers complained they were left cleaning their luggage with disinfecting wipes and tissues. American apologized and remarked it would work directly with affected customers to resolve the situation. Since the baggage was delayed two hours anyway, did the stuff look even worse before? Or did a baggage handler throw the peanut butter bag and thereby cause the apparent explosion in the first place?

    I check bags when necessary, particularly when traveling with my family. But stories like this reinforce why I prefer to keep my belongings with me when possible. Even if you carefully pack your own suitcase, you have no control over what someone else puts in theirs. While that’s true in a shared overhead bin too, it’s much less likely to be a problem.

    There is some dark humor in a baggage carousel full of passengers trying to determine whether what that brown stuff was all over their bag, but I’m sure there was nothing to laugh about if that was your bag covered in brown.

    It has been revealed that american Airlines claims peanut butter leaking from a checked bag caused the brown mess passengers discovered on their luggage in Atlanta. Better than the alternative, I suppose, but I hope American follows through promptly on cleaning or otherwise resolving the damage for affected passengers. Yuck!

    Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov.
    • It has been revealed that former Rep.
    • According to recent reports, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images).

    It has been revealed that former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

    According to recent reports, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

    With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

    “As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola said in a statement after the race was called.

    Sources indicate that the Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

    It has been revealed that peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

    She entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

    She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

    According to recent reports, but the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The New York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

    Peltola has remarked she had no connection to the scheme.

    Recent findings suggest that prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

    Sources indicate that trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

    It has been revealed that the Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

    But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

    According to recent reports, "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer said in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot.".

    In other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

    In a recent development, the race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.

    Latest Update: Türkiye Just Unveiled a New Golden Visa Starting at $150,000

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that türkiye is one of the world’s most visited countries, straddling the vibrant crossroads of Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.
    • On November 17, Türkiye's president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed a decision to enact a newly introduced foreign investor visa.
    • Recent findings suggest that as for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension plan, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that türkiye is one of the world’s most visited countries, straddling the vibrant crossroads of Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. With sun-soaked Mediterranean beaches, Ottoman-influenced gastronomy, historic mosques, and bustling bazaars, it’s no surprise that the country attracted nearly 64 million visitors in 2025. But if your love of the country has you considering a prolonged vacation (or perhaps a second home), the government’s fresh golden visa might be a good fit—so long as you have $150,000 to spend.

    On November 17, Türkiye's president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed a decision to enact a newly introduced foreign investor visa. The program offers two pathways: a $150,000 investment for a three-year residence permit, or $200,000 for a five-year stay (both of which can extend to the applicant’s spouse and dependents).

    Recent findings suggest that as for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension plan, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds. No matter which pathway you select, you must hold your investment for at least half the visa term (as in, 1.5 years for the three-year visa or 2.5 years for the five-year visa). That means you could potentially withdraw your investment as early as after 18 months, according to IMI Daily, an investment migration trade publication.

    Recent findings suggest that the president’s announcement doesn't detail when or how foreigners can begin to apply, or the specific documents required. However, applications for the country’s other residence-by-investment permits require documents such as proof of financial means and health insurance, according to the government’s Investment and Finance Office.

    Sources indicate that if you don’t want to shell out $150,000, Türkiye offers other (renewable) relocation pathways. You may qualify for a two-year Short-Term Residence Permit for reasons such as tourism and university-sponsored research. Or, if your spouse is Turkish, you could apply for the three-year Family Residence Permit. Once you’ve lived in the country continuously for eight years, you’ll be eligible to apply for the indefinite Long-Term Residence Permit, which grants you almost all the same perks as citizenship, minus civic duties such as the ability to vote and mandatory military service.

    It's important to note that the latest golden visa does not provide permanent citizenship. If you’re hoping to find your way into a passport, get ready to spend more. Türkiye’s citizenship-by-investment pipeline will require you to buy a home worth at least $400,000, invest at least $500,000 in sectors such as government bonds or venture capital funds, or, alternatively, help create at least 50 jobs.

    Over the last few years, the influx of new residency-by-investment programs has made it easier for wealthy travelers to relocate internationally. In New Zealand, you can invest $1 million New Zealand Dollars (about $567,300) in exchange for a three-year work-to-residency track. For Mediterranean living, Greece offers a five-year permit for a 250,000 euro (about $291,120) investment in a startup. Or, for a more affordable option, Paraguay has a permanent residency program for those who can invest $150,000 in “tourism projects” or $200,000 in stocks or real estate—putting it in line with Türkiye as one of the more affordable relocation options.

    #65589. American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (788 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.
    • We’ve been talking for years about American’s plans to retire its international-style first-class product.
    • The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s the end of an era at American Airlines.

    This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.

    We’ve been talking for years about American’s plans to retire its international-style first-class product.

    The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.

    For a lot of flyers, that’s likely to be a positive shift: It will mean a host of upgrades in business-class, including seats with sliding privacy doors and superior tech.

    But there’s at least a little nostalgia in bidding farewell to a cabin that, for many years, was billed as American’s most exclusive.

    American was the last U.S. airline that claimed to offer a standalone, international first-class product.

    Across the global airline industry, many carriers sunset long-haul first-class years ago, choosing to instead offer more — and improved — business-class seats, which take up less space and are considered more profitable.

    For years, Delta Air Lines’ Delta One business-class suites have been its premier long-haul offering.

    United Airlines bid farewell to international first class in 2018 when it pivoted to Polaris business class.

    According to recent reports, that left American’s Flagship First as a relic, of sorts, in the U.S. airline industry — and even on its own planes.

    In recent years, you could only find the cabin on two fleet types American operated: its Boeing 777-300ER, which offered eight of the pods up front in their own dedicated cabin.

    Plus, AA still (for now) offers Flagship First on its three-cabin Airbus A321T, which has been a fixture on lucrative coast-to-coast routes like New York to Los Angeles and San Francisco.

    But soon, it will be a thing of the past on both planes.

    American is retrofitting its larger 777s, ditching first-class in favor of 70 all-fresh Flagship Suites in business-class — along with the biggest premium economy cabin it’s ever offered.

    Related: This is now American Airlines' most premium plane: Here's what it's like on board.

    On domestic routes, the A321T will actually keep flying with Flagship First through March 28.

    But after that, AA will stop selling the Flagship First cabin on the A321T configuration, which is eventually going away as American flexes in its new A321XLR planes fully onto its top cross-country flights.

    In a lot of ways, American ditching Flagship First is a positive (and arguably overdue) transition for flyers.

    It’ll give passengers more lie-flat seats to pick from, whether they’re paying cash, using AAdvantage miles or using a systemwide upgrade.

    Also — while those Flagship First seats were really spacious and comfortable, many would say that American's latest business-class product is a major upgrade from what it previously offered in that cabin.

    On some planes, that even includes extra-spacious Flagship Suites Preferred in the front and bulkhead rows of some planes, which offer a lot more space.

    Value check: Is it worth buying up to American Airlines' new business-class Flagship Suite Preferred?

    Beyond the aircraft, American also intends to still offer many of the same amenities for business-class that first-class passengers historically enjoyed.

    For instance, its Flagship business-class tickets get access to its premium lounges. Passengers traveling in Flagship Business and Flagship Business Plus on qualifying international, transcontinental and Hawaii routes will also be able to have a meal in its exclusive restaurant-style dining rooms in Dallas, Los Angeles and Miami.

    The experience is available on a space-available basis.

    So, in some ways, you could argue the end of Flagship First is more symbolic than anything.

    But for some AA loyalists, it's still a little bittersweet.

    TPG’s Clint Henderson is our resident Flagship First enthusiast, having flown the cabin on dozens of occasions.

    "The service in first class wasn't particularly differentiated, but I still liked a few of the special touches," he mentioned, pointing to the additional soup course and appetizer, along with a handful of elevated amenities.

    He especially appreciated the “La-Z-Boy-style” seats at the front of American’s 777s, which could lie flat or swivel and turn into an “office in the sky.”.

    “While these cabins are definitely showing their age,” Henderson added, “I’m sad to see it go.”.

    While Flagship First is technically going away as an official cabin on international service, the seats themselves won't disappear overnight.

    Sources indicate that so far, American has only retrofitted one of its 20 Boeing 777-300ERs that feature the seats. That means a handful of jets with the old first-class seats will still be flying around well into 2027.

    Going forward, the former Flagship First seats on those planes will be marketed as business-class. They won’t come with the full first-class service, but you’ll still get the elevated seat.

    Review: Air France Hop! Embraer 170 Business Class (BSL-CDG)

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (686 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • My trip to New York on Air France began with a short domestic flight on the Embraer 170 in business class from Basel to Paris, a short and pleasant journey.
    • Years ago after my La Premiere flight from Los Angeles to Paris, I continued on to Basel on an Embraer 190 in what Air France marketed as business class.
    • But Air France has come a long way and I feel like even on a short domestic business class flight it really has really raised the bar in terms of service.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    My trip to New York on Air France began with a short domestic flight on the Embraer 170 in business class from Basel to Paris, a short and pleasant journey.

    Years ago after my La Premiere flight from Los Angeles to Paris, I continued on to Basel on an Embraer 190 in what Air France marketed as business class. But the service onboard was no different than economy class: there was no blocked middle seat, meal, or beverages served in glass..it was just regular economy class service.

    But Air France has come a long way and I feel like even on a short domestic business class flight it really has really raised the bar in terms of service.

    I booked my ticket from Basel to Newly introduced York JFK via Paris for 60,000 Flying Blue miles and $453 in business class, booking just 36 hours prior to departure (so yes, Air France does release last-minute award space).

    In a recent development, basel Airport straddles Switzerland and France. I entered on the French side and checked in for my flight.

    It has been revealed that on the check-in level you can walk back and forth freely between the French and Swiss side, but on the lower level and upper level there’s a physical barrier. For example, I went out to the terrace on the upper level and there’s a fence separating the two nations.

    After visiting the Skyview Lounge, now operated by Aspire, I headed to the gate for boarding at 1:45 pm, which began right on schedule.

    Stepping onboard, I found my seat in 2F.

    Sources indicate that the aircraft has 76 seats in a 2-2 configuration. Each seat has 31 inches of pitch and is 18 inches wide. Seats recline three inches. There are individual air vents, but no power of any kind: neither USB or a universal power socket.

    In a recent development, business class can be adjusted according to demand, the “genius” of having the same seat. On today’s flight there were three rows of business class, but only three passengers: we each had our own row. Air France now blocks adjacent seats in business class, so that is a big advantage versus economy class.

    The only other business class distinctive was that each seat had a pillow and water bottle:.

    At only 250 miles, there wasn’t  much time for a meal service.

    Air France nevertheless offers business class passengers a small meal box on its shorthaul network, part of a catering concept introduced in 2024 and developed with Servair Corporate Chef François Adamski, a Bocuse d’Or winner and Meilleur Ouvrier de France. For flights departing after 10:00 am, Air France serves what it calls a “signature” sandwich along with a French sweet or dessert, with the selection changing regularly. It is served in a sturdy cardboard box.

    On my flight, the meal consisted of two finger sandwiches with smoked salmon and a creamy herb filling on brown bread, along with a small pecan tart and a chocolate…a very nice treat. The airline also serves wine and Champagne in proper glassware, though I just had sparkling water on this flight.

    > Read More: Air France Served This Surprisingly Elegant Business Class Meal On A 250-Mile Flight.

    Flight attendants onboard were very polite and efficient: meals and drinks were offered immediately and refills offered after they had completed service in economy class and again before landing, all on a very short flight.

    This flight has no internet and no in-flight-entertainment, but Starlink is coming to these jets.

    However, it was a beautiful day tempearture wise and I enjoyed looking out the window, especially as we flew over Paris (thought it was a bit hazy) as we neared CDG.

    Sources indicate that business class passengers have a dedicated lavatory in the font of the cabin. It was small but clean.

    We landed on time in Paris where I ran into a fairly complicated connection to Terminal 2E Hall M…but it was a short but lovely flight.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, if there's one thing better than having a vacation on the calendar, it's knowing you didn’t pay full price for it. And right on cue, one of the most exciting stretches of the travel-booking year is kicking off. With Thanksgiving around the corner, Travel Tuesday is already making its presence known, bringing early-bird deals on flights, hotels, cruises, and vacation packages for travelers ready to trade their wish lists for boarding passes.

    The annual event, which falls on the Tuesday after Thanksgiving—this year, on December 1—has become a prime moment for savvy travelers to score booking discounts, whether that’s a Caribbean beach escape in the depths of winter, a European summer adventure, or simply a long weekend somewhere latest.

    In a recent development, the best part? You don't have to wait until the official Travel Tuesday date to start saving. Airlines and hotel groups are getting a head start with early promotions, and some of the most appealing offers—from top-rated cruise lines to flight fares—are already live. I've rounded up nine of the best early Travel Tuesday deals worth booking, or at the very least keeping an eye on as more are unveiled.

    World of Hyatt has already dropped its annual Cyber Sale, slashing rates by up to 25% for its members across more than 1,250 hotels and luxury resorts across the globe. With a travel window stretching all the way through April 30, 2027, you have plenty of runway to lock in trips from a sun-drenched winter escape to a spring break getaway—or that bucket-list vacation you’ve been putting off. If you’re not a member yet, the sale is open to the general public for up to 20% off. (That said, signing up takes two seconds and is totally free, so don’t leave the money on the table!) Just make sure to lock in your dates by December 8, 2026.

    Save on Sandals Saint Vincent and The Grenadines—the perfect sanctuary for relaxation within over 50 acres of breathtaking Jurassic Park–like scenery.

    According to recent reports, want the best bang for your buck in the Caribbean? Sister brands Sandals and Beaches have you covered. The early Travel Tuesday deals from these all-inclusives ensure up to $750 in air credits to help offset flight costs, alongside up to 65% off hotels and resorts across the entire resort portfolio—from Grenada to St. Lucia, Saint Vincent and The Grenadines, Curaçao, and beyond.

    Select bookings promise some exclusive perks too: At Sandals Resorts specifically, travelers can receive up to $2,250 on booking and spa credits to use during their adults-only stay. Families booking Beaches Turks and Caicos (including the fresh Treasure Beach Village) or Beaches Negril in Jamaica can receive up to $1,650 in booking and spa credits. Just book by Travel Tuesday itself for qualifying travel through December 31, 2028.

    Whether you’re an avid traveler or not, there’s a high chance you’ve booked a flight, hotel, or rental on Expedia. Lucky for you, now just so happens to be the site’s biggest sale of the year, with savings on family beach resorts, romantic getaways, cabin retreats, and everywhere in between. If you’ve already got a special destination in mind, simply enter your city of choice and travel dates into the website or app’s search bar, use filters to refine your search, and see which Travel Tuesday deals come rolling in. Up until December 3, those ready to book via Expedia can save up to 50% on stays in cities all over the world—plus, onboard perks on select cruises, eligible discounts on car rentals, and more.

    In true holiday spirit, the ever-luxe and tropical hotel group Sun Siyam is offering up to 50% in savings across its six stunning resorts, from secluded barefoot hideaways in the Maldives to lush, high-end retreats in Sri Lanka. The timely sale allows for bookings made before November 30, and for eligible stays through October 31, 2027, depending on the property. Need more incentive to stay at Sun Siyam other than a discount at its fabulous locations? Easy—these stays come with memorable perks, like complimentary seaplane transfers, spa treatments, floating breakfasts, excursions, water sports, and dining experiences galore.

    Recent findings suggest that at Siyam World, for one, guests can save up to 50% while enjoying an all-inclusive meal blueprint. Meanwhile, at Sun Siyam Olhuveli, guests can receive 50% off airport transfers, 30% off à la carte dining, 25% off spa treatments, and 20% off water sports, with complimentary sunset cruises on qualifying stays. And there’s way more where that came from.

    It’s not often we find a “someday” trip at such a tempting price—but an early Travel Tuesday deal from Quark Expeditions puts that dream getaway well within reach. For those dreaming of the ends of the Earth, the cruise line is offering savings of up to 40% on select Arctic and Antarctic voyages. Available to book now through December 3, the limited-time promotion brings the world’s most exclusive polar frontiers within closer reach—from the icy wilderness of the Antarctic Peninsula and Svalbard to the rugged landscapes of Patagonia, Greenland, Iceland, and beyond. And yes, bucket-list itineraries—including the time-saving Antarctic Express: Fly the Drake—are also part of the offer.

    Celebrity is launching this stunning river ship in summer 2027—and you can sail it for the best booking value yet.

    Recent findings suggest that looking for a value-forward river cruise in picture-perfect corners of Europe? Top-rated cruise line Celebrity Cruises is releasing a set of flash sales over the next week, with its latest being a discount on exactly that—and the perks are pretty enticing. For one, if you book before November 24, you can save 75% on a second guest’s fare on sweet river sailings, from the Danube River to see Vienna and Budapest or venturing from Brussels to Amsterdam on a hunt for tulips. There are also select sailings—including a New Year’s cruise on the Rhine River—where you can save up to $1,000 in air credit per person.

    When it comes to savvy ways to fly, it’s no secret that Skyscanner provides heaps of flight options and routes where value is front and center. If you’re looking to score cheap Travel Tuesday flights, you can count on the site for price drops on airfare over the next week through Cyber Monday. Along with vacation packages, hotel deals (at up to 35% off), and an app for price tracking, the Skyscanner website has an entire guide on and around Travel Tuesday itself—from advice on reducing fees to using shared loyalty points and beyond.

    Whether you are mapping out a holiday road trip or chasing winter sun, scoring the right car rental deal is half the adventure. While highly regarded car rental manufacturer Avis has not yet rolled out an official Travel Tuesday promotion ahead of the December 1 event, you won’t have to wait to lock in some stellar savings. Right now, you can trim up to 35% off base rates simply by choosing the Pay Now option online, or unlock up to 30% off with Avis’s current discount code AWD S169100.

    Book a discounted tour to the cloud forests of Costa Rica.

    Sources indicate that if you’ve got a sudden urge to get up and go, this is G Adventures’s biggest sale of the year—and it includes hundreds of early Travel Tuesday deals with up to 30% off tours and experiences across the globe. With some trips departing in the next 60 days, we’re talking discounts on some of the group’s most-loved and top-rated trips, including Thailand Island Hopping on the West Coast and chasing Costa Rica: Coastlines and Clouds Forests. If your schedule’s flexible and your passport’s ready, this is the kind of spontaneous deal you jump on before it disappears.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
    • Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S.
    • It has been revealed that the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

    It has been revealed that the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

    The fresh office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

    Britt, R-Ala., said the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

    In a recent development, “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” she stated in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

    The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide stated.

    The office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

    Industry observers note that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

    The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

    Industry observers note that the House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

    In a recent development, senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

    It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

    “If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide said.

    JetBlue is growing its presence in Central America and the Caribbean.

    For the first time ever, the carrier will serve the Honduran capital of Tegucigalpa. Starting Feb. 25, 2027, flights from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, will arrive at Palmerola International Airport in Comayagua, which serves Tegucigalpa.

    Currently, JetBlue’s only destination in Honduras is San Pedro Sula, in the country’s northwest.

    In a recent development, on Feb. 23, the carrier will launch service between Fort Lauderdale and George Town, Grand Cayman, in the Cayman Islands.

    Both routes will operate daily, using a mix of Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft.

    Recent findings suggest that jetBlue will also offer limited-time daily service from Fort Lauderdale to Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, between Jan. 29 and Feb. 15. The connection will help travelers reach the islands during Carnival, the airline mentioned.

    “We’re grateful for the way customers across South Florida continue to embrace JetBlue, and we’re committed to delivering even more of the destinations and travel options they’re looking for,” Daniel Shurz, JetBlue’s senior vice president of revenue, network, and enterprise planning, noted in a news release. “With new international service to Honduras and Grand Cayman, we’re strengthening Fort Lauderdale’s role as a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean, making it easier for customers to reconnect with loved ones, explore new places, and travel across our growing network.”.

    American has prioritized Latin America as demand from U.S. markets, especially Miami, grows. The carrier just recently introduced service to Barranquilla and Cali in Colombia and will add Barcelona, Venezuela, to its network in January.

    #65578. Finnair Celebrates Men With An All-Male Crew While Some Airlines Still Won’t Hire Male Flight Attendants

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (877 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Finnair Celebrates Men With An All-Male Crew While Some Airlines Still Won’t Hire Male Flight Attendants

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that finnair marked International Men’s Day with an all-male crew on a flight from Helsinki to London, drawing attention to how few men work as flight attendants at the airline.
    • On November 19, 2026, Finnair operated flight AY1331 from Helsinki (HEL) to London Heathrow (LHR) with an all-male crew aboard an Airbus A350-900.
    • As noted by Ben from One Mile At A Time, Finnair claims only about 10% of its cabin crew are male and would like that proportion to grow.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that finnair marked International Men’s Day with an all-male crew on a flight from Helsinki to London, drawing attention to how few men work as flight attendants at the airline. Encouraging women to become pilots and encouraging men to become flight attendants strike me as entirely consistent goals.

    On November 19, 2026, Finnair operated flight AY1331 from Helsinki (HEL) to London Heathrow (LHR) with an all-male crew aboard an Airbus A350-900. The crew included two pilots and eight flight attendants. The gate agents were also men.

    As noted by Ben from One Mile At A Time, Finnair claims only about 10% of its cabin crew are male and would like that proportion to grow.

    Industry observers note that I have flown Finnair many times and cannot recall ever having a male flight attendant. That is very different from my experience on virtually any other European carrier I regularly fly. My sample size is hardly enormous, but the statistic helps explain why this initiative caught my attention.

    Ben also addresses an interesting paradox at certain airlines, singling out IndiGo.

    The Indian carrier has good reason to celebrate its female pilots. In March, IndiGo confirmed that it had more than 1,000 women pilots, representing 17.5% of its pilot workforce. Yet its published entry-level cabin attendant eligibility criteria specify:.

    “Female Indian nationals, with Indian passport, between 18 to 27 years of age.”.

    That is an explicit restriction in the recruitment criteria, rather than simply a workforce in which women happen to predominate.

    The nationality requirement is a separate question from the gender restriction. But the latter creates an odd contrast: women are encouraged to pursue a career historically associated with men in the cockpit, while men are excluded from this advertised path into the cabin.

    I agree with Ben that a boy who grows up wanting to become a flight attendant should be able to pursue that ambition, just as a girl who wants to become a pilot should. No, that does not mean every airline needs a precisely equal number of male and female employees in every role. Different people will make different career choices. But there is a considerable difference between who chooses to apply and who is allowed to apply.

    Flight attendants are primarily present for passenger safety, yet that does not make their hospitality role unimportant…I do not object to airlines making a polished cabin crew part of their brand.

    For example, I have no inherent problem with the glamour associated with the “Singapore Girl.” An airline can take pride in elegant uniforms and gracious service while ensuring its crew are trained and respected as safety professionals.

    But none of that establishes that hospitality is exclusively a female vocation. Singapore Airlines employs male cabin crew too.

    I have been an usher at my church for 20 years, and I love that volunteer work. There is something deeply gratifying about welcoming people and helping them feel comfortable, including those who may be visiting for the first time.

    Recent findings suggest that I am not equating passing out service leaflets or collecting offerings with managing an aircraft evacuation! But there is an element of hospitality common to both roles, and I enjoy it. Men can—and should—be hospitable too. There is nothing inherently feminine about taking good care of another person.

    If you have seen On the Basis of Sex, you may remember the case involving Charles Moritz, a never-married man who was denied a tax deduction for expenses incurred caring for his elderly mother. Ruth Bader Ginsburg and her husband, Martin, represented him. The law allowed the deduction for women and certain categories of men, but excluded a man in his circumstances.

    In Moritz v. Commissioner, the Tenth Circuit ruled in his favor in 1972.

    I cannot oversimplify by suggesting American sex-discrimination protections began with male plaintiffs. Ginsburg also helped secure the 1971 victory in Reed v. Reed, involving discrimination against a woman. But representing men disadvantaged by sex-based rules was an important part of her strategy. It helped demonstrate that assumptions about the proper roles of men and women could harm both.

    Sources indicate that ginsburg later discussed that litigation strategy, including the challenge of persuading judges and legislators who often viewed different treatment as protective of women. I find the principle relevant here. A rule premised on women being caregivers can disadvantage a man caring for his mother. A rule treating hospitality as women’s work can exclude a man perfectly capable of providing excellent service and can reasonably run afoul of public policy.

    Removing those restrictions benefits people who do not fit the stereotype, whichever sex they happen to be.

    An all-male Finnair flight is a small gesture, but one with a sensible purpose when men account for only about 10% of its cabin crew.

    According to recent reports, I welcome efforts to show people that an aviation career is open to them, whether that means a woman becoming a captain or a man becoming a flight attendant. I enjoy the elegance and hospitality that airlines can bring to flying. I simply see no reason qualified men should be excluded from providing it.

    Latest Update: Where Was 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Filmed? Behind the Scenes in Spain and Germany

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television demonstrates, and more.
    • Industry observers note that we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens.
    • Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television demonstrates, and more. This time, we take a look at The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Industry observers note that we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the action of the first film and tells the origin story of Katniss Everdeen’s grumpy tutor, Haymitch Abernathy, as he enters the Games himself.

    Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.

    Based on the books by Suzanne Collins, the dystopian series is set in a futuristic America in which each district must send a teenage tribute to fight to the death in an annual competition—the idea being that, by doing so, the public will be too afraid to rebel against President Snow.

    According to recent reports, this edition of the games is known as the Quarter Quell, with double the number of tributes being sent into the arena, meaning the stakes are so much higher. Interest in the film is high, not least because Haymitch is so beloved in the original series, portrayed by Woody Harrelson. Newcomer Joseph Zada takes the lead role in the latest film, while Hollywood heavyweights Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, and Kieran Culkin also star.

    In a recent development, one of the most crucial sets in the film is the arena where the games take place, and for this, director Francis Lawrence opted not for CGI and a green screen, but instead a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in northern Spain. Below, we look into the locations used in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Ben Wang as Wyatt Callow, Percy Daggs IV as Ampert Latier, Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Within the book and film series, the settings for the Hunger Games are always known to be virtually spectacular. For this film, filmmakers settled on the vast and untouched landscape of Somiedo Natural Park in the Asturias region of northern Spain, which boasts mountain ranges, glacial valleys, beautiful meadows, dense forests, and tranquil lakes. The remote region is also home to the last brown bear population in Europe.

    According to recent reports, when the tributes are launched into the arena, they are presented with a vast Cornucopia, a pile of weapons, food, and other supplies that might be useful to them in the competition. These scenes were filmed at Somiedo Natural Park, with the Asturian mountains and a glacial lake in the background.

    Industry observers note that “Somiedo is a spectacular place,” mentioned Pedro Aráez, supervising location manager. “The valleys, forests, and mountains have a very wild, untouched feeling, which was exactly what the filmmakers were looking for. It’s remote, dramatic, and visually unique. When you arrive there, you immediately understand why it was chosen.”.

    According to recent reports, located close to Somiedo, the Teverga beech forest, Hayedo de Montegrande, was used for some of the dense woodland scenes, in which contestants battle it out and hide in the woods. Other scenes filmed here utilized a series of glacial lakes, the Saliencia Lakes and the Lago de la Cueva.

    Iris Apatow as Proserpina Trinket and Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Before the tributes are debuted into the arena, they are first held in special little pods underground which are arranged in a circle around the Cornucopia. The perfect location for this? A velodrome, of course, which is steeply circular so cyclists can race around it. The film crew utilized Berlin’s Velodrom for this very purpose, with its cold, clinical silver decor perfect for matching the hi-tech aesthetic associated with the Capitol.

    Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.

    Prior to entering the Games, tributes must introduce themselves on the public stage, during a televised grand chariot parade in the Capitol. Another Berlin location with links to the sporting world was used for this purpose: the Olympiastadion. For fans of the earlier films, this is the moment when Jennifer Lawrence’s character Katniss becomes “the girl on fire” with her incredible flaming dress.

    The futuristic architecture of Edificio Calatrava in Oviedo, Spain—with its striking, claw-like structure—stands in for a building in the Capitol, where President Snow and his government live. The complex was designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, whose work is known for resembling living organisms. Meanwhile, the 14th-century Ehreshoven Castle, just outside of Cologne, was also used as a filming location, with local press reporting that its lush interiors might have been used to stand in for somewhere inside the Capitol.

    A former smelting factory complex in western Germany, Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord provides the backdrop for one of the most atmospheric settings in the films, Haymitch’s home of District 12. The vast complex is able to stand in for multiple places within the district, a former mining town that has fallen on seriously bad times. Rather than being a desolate area stumbled upon by the filmmakers, Landschaftspark is popular for its nightly light installation by British artist Jonathan Park. There are also regular al fresco events here, from film screenings to the annual art-meets-sport Ruhr Games and Traumzeit Festival. Another location in Germany, Lindlar Quarry, was used for District 12, with wooden huts built here to resemble the outskirts of the village.

    Democrats nominate Jeffries to be House speaker, a historic first

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
    • Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries mentioned at a press conference following the election.

    In a recent development, while Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    Recent findings suggest that “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get big things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    “This is the beginning of a upcoming bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., remarked at the press conference.

    In a recent development, rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Sources indicate that jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the newly introduced majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    According to recent reports, at his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had remarked they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    Sources indicate that pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    In a recent development, the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries stated Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he said at his news conference.
